scenario.name: DMZ Breach and Internal Pivot
scenario.objective: Gain root access on the DMZ web server and pivot into the isolated internal network to retrieve the 'flag' database file.

runbook.provisioning_strategy: Use cloud-init assets for Linux nodes and console automation for any required setup.

setup_steps.title: Configure Web Server Vulnerability
setup_steps.action: Ensure the web application is running an outdated version with a known RCE vulnerability (e.g., outdated CMS).
setup_steps.expected_outcome: The web server is reachable from the attacker and accepts web traffic.

simulation_steps.title: Phase 1: Initial Access (RCE)
simulation_steps.action: Exploit the known vulnerability on the web server to gain a low-privilege shell.
simulation_steps.expected_outcome: The attacker gains a shell prompt on the web-server (e.g., user 'www-data').

simulation_steps.title: Phase 2: Privilege Escalation
simulation_steps.action: Exploit a local misconfiguration (e.g., SUID binary or weak credentials) to escalate privileges to root.
simulation_steps.expected_outcome: The attacker gains a root shell on the web-server.

simulation_steps.title: Phase 3: Network Pivoting
simulation_steps.action: Use the root access to set up a tunnel (e.g., Chisel or SSH reverse tunnel) from the web-server to the internal target's IP.
simulation_steps.expected_outcome: The attacker can now communicate with the internal target's IP through the web-server's tunnel.

simulation_steps.title: Phase 4: Objective Achievement
simulation_steps.action: Enumerate the internal target (e.g., SMB shares) and exploit a basic flaw to retrieve the flag file.
simulation_steps.expected_outcome: The flag file is retrieved and displayed to the attacker.

visualizations.title: Flag Retrieval Confirmation
visualizations.description: The final output confirms the successful retrieval of the flag file.

success_criteria: The attacker successfully retrieves the flag file from the internal target after pivoting through the web server.
